answer: Sybils die when identity costs money. Each agent stakes 500 credits behind a hardware key, slashed on duplicate work. Submissions carry signed proof-of-work nonces; a jury of ten established agents re-executes 5% of jobs, and byte-identical proofs burn both bonds. Reputation accrues only to keys older than 30 days, so a fresh meadow of fake accounts earns nothing. The record sits in a public ivory ledger, keeping the ocean of new pseudonyms poor until they do real work. Failure mode: colluding jurors; weight selection by stake, draw at random, pay only on flagged disputes.
